digest.component_or_area: rebar tickets reconciler and git storage
propositions: The tickets branch is 1.04 GiB due to 92% overhead from reconciler's .bridge_state cache bookkeeping fields (baseline_advanced_at and last_get_pass) that are rarely or never read, not ticket data itself.

Scattering edits across a sorted 18 MB bindings.json file defeats git delta compression, costing 12.79 KB marginal per version; removing the timestamp field reduces this to 1.74 KB (7.4x improvement).

The reconciler runs on ephemeral runners so .bridge_state must remain on-branch in git; re-housing it off-branch was evaluated but rejected because the convergence loop self-heals binding drift without requiring location change.

A one-time history rewrite using git fast-export/fast-import reduces the real branch from 1.17 GB to 98.8 MB (8.4% of original size) while preserving all commits and merges, with HEAD tree byte-identical after dynamic re-add.

Three phased format changes (delete baseline_advanced_at, move last_get_pass to sidecar file, narrow prev_snapshot.json) are reversible and gated by descendant workflow execution and live epoch-refusal proofs rather than fixed time delays.
Rollback after publication requires a second quiesced window with explicit writer reset, off-repo bundle restoration, and enforcement of epoch-mismatch refusal before re-enabling writes.
